learn.hook: The blackboard, your maths notebook, a door, and the paper kite you fly on Makar Sankranti are all quadrilaterals. But they are not all the same kind!
points: A quadrilateral is a closed figure with 4 straight sides, 4 vertices, 4 angles and 2 diagonals.
A trapezium has a pair of parallel sides. A parallelogram has both pairs of opposite sides parallel.
A rectangle is a parallelogram with all four angles 90°. A rhombus is a parallelogram with all four sides equal.
A square has all sides equal and all angles 90°, so every square is a rectangle and also a rhombus.
A kite has two pairs of equal sides, and each pair sits next to each other (adjacent).

example.q: A quadrilateral has all four sides 5 cm, and one of its angles is 90°. Which quadrilateral is it?
steps: All sides equal, so it is a rhombus, which is a parallelogram
In a parallelogram, opposite angles are equal and neighbouring angles add to 180°
So one 90° angle makes all four angles 90°
All sides equal and all angles 90° means a square

learn.reallife: Carpenters check that a door frame is a true rectangle, and rangoli makers love rhombus and kite patterns.

games.title: Name that quadrilateral
pairs: only one pair of parallel sides

games.title: Family of shapes
items: Every square is a rectangle.
A square has four right angles and opposite sides equal, so it is a special rectangle.
Every rectangle is a square.
A 4 cm by 7 cm rectangle does not have all sides equal.
Every rhombus is a parallelogram.
A rhombus has both pairs of opposite sides parallel.
A kite always has 4 equal sides.
A kite needs only two pairs of equal neighbouring sides, like 3, 3, 5, 5.
Every square is a rhombus.
A square has all four sides equal.
A quadrilateral has 3 diagonals.
A quadrilateral has exactly 2 diagonals.

quiz.q: Which quadrilateral has all four sides equal and all four angles equal to 90°?
quiz.explain: A square has equal sides like a rhombus and right angles like a rectangle.
steps: We need all 4 sides equal AND all 4 angles 90°.
A rhombus has equal sides but need not have right angles; a rectangle has right angles but need not have equal sides.
quiz.mistake: Picks rhombus, forgetting that a rhombus need not have right angles

quiz.q: How many diagonals does a quadrilateral have?
quiz.explain: Each vertex joins only the opposite vertex by a diagonal. That gives 2 diagonals, like AC and BD.
steps: From A: only AC is a diagonal
AC and BD are counted once each: 2
quiz.mistake: Counts each diagonal twice or confuses diagonals with sides

quiz.q: Arjun's paper kite has sides 30 cm, 30 cm, 45 cm and 45 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: Perimeter is the sum of all four sides: 30 + 30 + 45 + 45 = 150 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds only two sides (75 cm)

quiz.q: A quadrilateral has opposite sides parallel and all angles 90°. Its neighbouring sides are 4 cm and 7 cm. What is it?
quiz.explain: Four right angles with unequal neighbouring sides make a rectangle, not a square.
steps: Opposite sides parallel and all angles 90° → a rectangle (or a square).
The neighbouring sides 4 cm and 7 cm are unequal, so it is not a square.
quiz.mistake: Calls every shape with right angles a square

quiz.q: Which statement is true?
quiz.explain: A square has all four sides equal, so it is always a rhombus. A rhombus need not have right angles, so it is not always a square.
steps: A square has all four sides equal, so it is always a rhombus.
A rhombus need not have right angles, and a rectangle need not have equal sides.
A kite need not have parallel sides. So 'Every square is a rhombus' is true.
Answer: Every square is a rhombus
quiz.mistake: Reverses the 'special case' relationship between square and rhombus

quiz.q: One side of a rhombus is 6 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: All four sides of a rhombus are equal, so the perimeter is 4 × 6 = 24 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses only two sides, or squares the side (36)

quiz.q: Which quadrilateral can have exactly one pair of parallel sides?
quiz.explain: Parallelograms, rhombuses and rectangles always have two pairs of parallel sides. A trapezium can have just one pair.
steps: Parallelograms, rhombuses and rectangles always have two pairs of parallel sides.
A trapezium only needs one pair of parallel sides.
So a trapezium can have exactly one pair.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a rhombus or rectangle has only one pair of parallel sides

quiz.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 80°, 95° and 110°. What is the fourth angle?
quiz.explain: The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°. 80 + 95 + 110 = 285, and 360 − 285 = 75°.
quiz.mistake: Uses 180° (the triangle angle sum) or makes an adding slip

teach.ask: Gappu chirps: My friend says a square is a rectangle. That sounds wrong! Is it?
teach.praise: Yes! A square has four right angles and equal opposite sides, so it is a special kind of rectangle. Thanks!
teach.nudge: What does a shape need to be a rectangle? Does a square have those things?

revise.summary: A quadrilateral has 4 sides, 4 angles and 2 diagonals. Trapeziums have a pair of parallel sides, parallelograms have two pairs, and rectangles, rhombuses and squares are special parallelograms; a kite has two pairs of equal neighbouring sides.
focus: Name quadrilaterals from their sides and angles
Know which shapes are special cases of others
Find perimeters of kites and rhombuses
Find a missing angle using the 360° sum
remember: Trapezium: a pair of parallel sides; parallelogram: both pairs
Rectangle: parallelogram with all angles 90°; rhombus: parallelogram with all sides equal
Square: all sides equal and all angles 90° (a rectangle and a rhombus)
Kite: two pairs of equal sides next to each other
traps: Every square is a rhombus, but not every rhombus is a square
Right angles alone don't make a square: check the sides
Angles of a quadrilateral add to 360°, not 180°

learn.hook: Start with just one rule — 'all four angles are right angles' — and you can prove everything else about a rectangle. Like a detective!
points: Definition: a rectangle is a quadrilateral with four right angles. Everything else is deduced from this.
Opposite sides are parallel: the two angles on one side add to 90° + 90° = 180°, and when co-interior angles add to 180°, the lines are parallel.
Opposite sides are equal: the diagonal AC splits rectangle ABCD into triangles ABC and CDA, which are congruent (AC is common and the alternate angles are equal). So AB = CD and BC = DA.
If a quadrilateral has three right angles, the fourth is 360° − 270° = 90°, so it must be a rectangle.
The diagonals are equal and bisect each other, so OA = OB = OC = OD. That makes triangles like AOB isosceles — handy for finding angles.

example.q: In rectangle ABCD the diagonals meet at O and ∠OAB = 30°. Find ∠OBA and ∠AOB.

learn.reallife: Carpenters check a door frame is a true rectangle by measuring both diagonals — if they are equal, the corners are right angles.

items.text: Three angles are 90°, so the fourth is ___

games.title: Prove it!
items: A rectangle's opposite sides are parallel because co-interior angles add to 180°.
The diagonal of a rectangle makes two congruent triangles.
ΔABC ≅ ΔCDA.
A quadrilateral with three right angles might have a fourth angle of 100°.
In a rectangle, the triangles formed by the diagonals at O are always equilateral.
They are isosceles; equilateral only when the angle at O is 60°.

quiz.q: A quadrilateral has three right angles. What is its fourth angle?
quiz.explain: The angles add to 360°, so the fourth is 360° − 3 × 90° = 90°.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the angle sum of a quadrilateral is 360°

quiz.q: Why are the opposite sides of a rectangle parallel?
options: Because all four sides are equal
The two angles on the same side add up to 180°
quiz.explain: Each pair of neighbouring angles is 90° + 90° = 180°. Co-interior angles adding to 180° means the lines are parallel.
steps: Answer: The two angles on the same side add up to 180°
quiz.mistake: Uses a property that has not yet been proved

quiz.q: In rectangle ABCD the diagonals meet at O and ∠OAB = 35°. What is ∠OBA?
quiz.explain: OA = OB, so triangle OAB is isosceles and its base angles are equal: ∠OBA = 35°.
quiz.mistake: Takes the complement 90° − 35° instead

quiz.q: In rectangle ABCD the diagonals meet at O and ∠OAB = 35°. What is ∠AOB?
quiz.mistake: Assumes the diagonals of a rectangle meet at 90°

quiz.q: In rectangle ABCD the diagonals meet at O and ∠OAB = 35°. What is ∠OAD?
quiz.mistake: Thinks the diagonal bisects the right angle

quiz.q: In rectangle ABCD, diagonal AC = 10 cm. The diagonals meet at O. How long is OB?
quiz.explain: The diagonals are equal (BD = 10 cm) and bisect each other, so OB = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the diagonals bisect each other

quiz.q: To show that opposite sides of rectangle ABCD are equal, which triangles do we prove congruent?
options: ΔABC and ΔCDA, made by diagonal AC
quiz.explain: Diagonal AC splits the rectangle into ΔABC and ΔCDA. They are congruent, so AB = CD and BC = DA.
steps: Answer: ΔABC and ΔCDA, made by diagonal AC
quiz.mistake: Uses triangles that do not contain both pairs of sides

quiz.q: In rectangle ABCD the diagonals meet at O and ∠AOB = 60°. If AB = 4 cm, how long is diagonal AC?
quiz.explain: OA = OB and ∠AOB = 60°, so the base angles are 60° too: triangle AOB is equilateral. OA = AB = 4 cm, and AC = 2 × OA = 8 cm.
quiz.mistake: Stops at OA instead of doubling to get the full diagonal

teach.ask: Gappu says: 'A rectangle has opposite sides equal — everyone just knows that.' How can you PROVE it?
teach.praise: Ooh, a proof! The diagonal makes two congruent triangles, so the matching sides must be equal.
teach.nudge: What could you draw inside the rectangle to make two triangles?

revise.summary: A rectangle is defined as a quadrilateral with four right angles, and its other properties are proved from this. Its opposite sides are parallel and equal, and its diagonals are equal and bisect each other, making isosceles triangles.
focus: Prove opposite sides of a rectangle are parallel and equal
Show that three right angles force the fourth
Use OA = OB = OC = OD to find angles at the diagonals
Find diagonal lengths from half-diagonals
remember: Rectangle: a quadrilateral with four right angles
Co-interior angles 90° + 90° = 180° → opposite sides parallel
Diagonal AC gives congruent triangles ABC and CDA → opposite sides equal
Diagonals are equal and bisect each other: OA = OB = OC = OD
traps: The diagonals of a rectangle do not always meet at 90°
A diagonal does not bisect the right angle of a rectangle
Don't stop at half the diagonal when asked for the full one

learn.hook: Cross two sticks, join their ends with a thread — and you have made a quadrilateral. Which one? It depends on how you cross the sticks!
points: Two equal lines that bisect each other (at any angle) give a rectangle when their ends are joined. Two equal sticks tied at their midpoints with a thread around the ends make a right angle at every corner.
Draw two perpendicular diameters of a circle and join their ends: you get a square, because the diagonals are equal, bisect each other and meet at 90°.
Any two lines that bisect each other give a parallelogram. If they bisect each other at right angles (but are unequal), you get a rhombus.
Kite from its diagonals: make one diagonal the perpendicular bisector of the other, but do not cut the first one in half.
Square from one diagonal, without a protractor: draw diagonal AC, construct its perpendicular bisector with a compass, then mark B and D on it at a distance of half of AC from the centre.

example.q: Diagonals of 8 cm and 8 cm bisect each other at 50°. Which quadrilateral do you get?
steps: So it is a rectangle (not a square)

learn.reallife: Kite makers tie two sticks in a cross before pasting the paper — how they cross them decides the shape of the kite!

games.title: Diagonals decide the shape
pairs: Equal, bisect each other, not at 90°

One is the perpendicular bisector of the other only

items: Draw the diagonal AC
Construct the perpendicular bisector of AC with a compass

quiz.q: Diagonals of 6 cm and 10 cm bisect each other at right angles. Which quadrilateral is formed?
quiz.explain: Diagonals that bisect each other at 90° give a rhombus; they are unequal, so it is not a square.
quiz.mistake: Thinks perpendicular diagonals always make a square

quiz.q: Diagonals of 7 cm and 7 cm bisect each other at right angles. Which quadrilateral is formed?
options: Rhombus that is not a square
Rectangle that is not a square
Kite that is not a rhombus
quiz.explain: Equal diagonals give a rectangle; perpendicular bisecting diagonals give a rhombus. Both together: a square.
quiz.mistake: Notices only one of the two properties

quiz.q: Diagonals of 5 cm and 9 cm bisect each other at 70°. Which quadrilateral is formed?
quiz.explain: Diagonals that only bisect each other (unequal, not perpendicular) give a general parallelogram.
steps: Not equal, not 90° → nothing more special
quiz.mistake: Assumes any crossing diagonals make a rhombus

quiz.q: Two perpendicular diameters of a circle with radius 5 cm are joined at their ends. How long is each diagonal of the square formed?
quiz.explain: Each diagonal is a diameter: 2 × 5 = 10 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses the radius as the diagonal

quiz.q: To build a square from a 6 cm diagonal AC, how far from the centre O should B and D be marked?
quiz.explain: A square's diagonals are equal and bisect each other, so OB = OD = OA = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm.
quiz.mistake: Marks B and D at the full diagonal length

quiz.q: Diagonal BD is cut into two equal parts of 4 cm by diagonal AC at right angles, but AC is split into 3 cm and 7 cm. What shape is ABCD?
quiz.explain: AC is the perpendicular bisector of BD, but BD does not bisect AC. That is a kite.
steps: AC itself is not bisected → kite
quiz.mistake: Thinks the shape must be a rhombus because the diagonals are perpendicular

quiz.q: Ravi crosses two equal sticks at their midpoints and stretches a thread around their ends. What angle does the thread make at each corner?
quiz.explain: Equal diagonals that bisect each other give a rectangle, so every corner is a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the corner angle depends on how the sticks are crossed

quiz.q: Which pair of diagonals can NEVER make a rectangle?
options: Diagonals of 6 cm and 6 cm crossing at their midpoints
Diagonals of 9 cm and 9 cm crossing at their midpoints at 30°
Diagonals of 4 cm and 4 cm crossing at their midpoints at 90°
quiz.explain: A rectangle's diagonals must be equal. 5 cm and 8 cm are unequal, so they can never form a rectangle.
steps: A rectangle's diagonals must be equal and bisect each other.
5 cm and 8 cm are unequal, so they can never make a rectangle.
The others are equal diagonals bisecting each other (the 90° pair makes a square, which is also a rectangle).
Answer: Diagonals of 5 cm and 8 cm
quiz.mistake: Forgets that a square is also a rectangle

teach.ask: Gappu has two equal straws and some string. How can he make a rectangle without a protractor?
teach.praise: Cross them at their middles and tie the ends! Equal diagonals that bisect each other make a rectangle.
teach.nudge: Where should the two straws cross each other?

revise.summary: The diagonals decide the shape: lines that bisect each other give a parallelogram, equal ones a rectangle, perpendicular ones a rhombus, and equal perpendicular ones a square. A kite has one diagonal as the perpendicular bisector of the other.
focus: Name the quadrilateral formed from given diagonals
Build a square from perpendicular diameters of a circle
Construct a square from one diagonal without a protractor
Build a kite from its diagonals
remember: Bisect each other → parallelogram
Equal and bisect each other → rectangle
Bisect each other at 90° → rhombus; also equal → square
Kite: one diagonal is the perpendicular bisector of the other
traps: Perpendicular diagonals alone don't make a square: they must also be equal
A rectangle needs equal diagonals; unequal ones never make one
Don't think both diagonals of a kite are cut in half; only one is

learn.hook: Draw any quadrilateral at all, even a wonky one. Tear off its four corners and put them together: they always make a full turn of 360°!
points: The angles of every quadrilateral add up to 360°, because a diagonal splits it into two triangles: 180° + 180°.
Rectangle: the diagonals are equal and bisect each other.
Rhombus: the diagonals bisect each other at right angles (they are perpendicular), and each diagonal bisects the angles at its ends.
Square: the diagonals are equal, perpendicular and bisect each other. It has every property of a rectangle and a rhombus.
Kite: the diagonals are perpendicular, and one diagonal cuts the other in half.

example.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are x, 2x, 3x and 4x. Find each angle.

learn.reallife: Tile makers and architects use the 360° rule to check that floor tiles and window frames fit together with no gaps.

games.title: Always true for a rectangle?
buckets: Not always true for a rectangle
items: Diagonals are equal
All angles are 90°
Diagonals bisect each other
Opposite sides are parallel
All sides are equal
Diagonals are perpendicular
Diagonals bisect the corner angles
Neighbouring sides are equal

games.title: From general to special
games.prompt: Each shape is a special kind of the one before it. Start with the most general.
items: Quadrilateral
Parallelogram
Rhombus
Square

quiz.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 90°, 90° and 120°. What is the fourth angle?
quiz.explain: The four angles add up to 360°. 90 + 90 + 120 = 300, so the fourth angle is 360 − 300 = 60°.
quiz.mistake: Assumes the missing angle must also be 90°

quiz.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are x, 2x, 3x and 4x. What is the largest angle?
quiz.explain: 10x = 360°, so x = 36° and the largest angle is 4x = 144°.
quiz.mistake: Stops at x = 36° and forgets to find 4x

quiz.q: In rectangle ABCD, diagonal AC is 13 cm. How long is diagonal BD?
quiz.explain: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal, so BD = AC = 13 cm.
steps: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal.
BD = 13 cm (6.5 cm is only half of it).
quiz.mistake: Halves the diagonal, mixing up 'equal' with 'bisect each other'

quiz.q: At what angle do the diagonals of a rhombus cross each other?
quiz.explain: The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular, so they always cross at 90°.
steps: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the angle depends on the side length

quiz.q: Which quadrilateral always has diagonals that are equal AND perpendicular?
quiz.explain: A rectangle has equal diagonals and a rhombus has perpendicular ones. Only a square always has both.
steps: Rectangle: diagonals equal. Rhombus: diagonals perpendicular.
A square has every property of both.
So only a square always has diagonals that are equal AND perpendicular.
quiz.mistake: Remembers only one of the two diagonal properties

quiz.q: Why do the angles of any quadrilateral add up to 360°?
options: It always has four right angles
A diagonal splits it into two triangles, and 180° + 180° = 360°
Every quadrilateral fits exactly inside a circle
Its four sides add up to 360
quiz.explain: Each triangle has an angle sum of 180°. A diagonal cuts any quadrilateral into two triangles, so the total is 360°.
steps: A diagonal cuts any quadrilateral into two triangles.
Each triangle's angles add up to 180°.
Answer: A diagonal splits it into two triangles, and 180° + 180° = 360°
quiz.mistake: Thinks the rule only works because squares have four 90° angles

quiz.q: In rhombus PQRS, ∠P = 120°. The diagonal PR bisects ∠P. What angle does PR make with side PQ?
quiz.explain: A diagonal of a rhombus bisects the angle at its end, so it splits 120° into two angles of 60°.
quiz.mistake: Confuses 'bisects the angle' with 'is perpendicular'

quiz.q: Aisha draws a quadrilateral whose diagonals bisect each other at right angles but are NOT equal. What shape is it?
quiz.explain: Diagonals that bisect each other at 90° make a rhombus. Since they are not equal, it cannot be a square.
steps: Diagonals that bisect each other at right angles make a rhombus.
They are not equal, so it is not a square.
In a kite only one diagonal is cut in half, so the answer is Rhombus.
quiz.mistake: Picks kite, but in a kite only one diagonal is cut in half

teach.ask: Gappu wonders: My quadrilateral is all crooked. How can its angles still add up to 360°?
teach.praise: Cut it with a diagonal into two triangles, each with 180°, so 360° in total. It works for any shape!
teach.nudge: What happens if you draw a line from one corner to the opposite corner? What shapes do you get?

revise.summary: The angles of any quadrilateral add up to 360°, since a diagonal splits it into two triangles. Rectangles have equal diagonals that bisect each other, rhombuses have perpendicular ones that bisect each other, and squares have both.
focus: Find missing angles using the 360° sum
Solve angle problems like x, 2x, 3x, 4x
Use diagonal properties of rectangles, rhombuses, squares and kites
Use the fact that a rhombus diagonal bisects its angles
remember: Angle sum of a quadrilateral = 360° (180° + 180°)
Rectangle: diagonals equal and bisect each other
Rhombus: diagonals bisect each other at 90° and bisect the angles
Square: diagonals equal, perpendicular and bisect each other
traps: Don't stop at x: find the angle asked for
Equal diagonals is not the same as bisecting each other
Perpendicular, bisecting but unequal diagonals give a rhombus, not a square or kite

learn.hook: Push a rectangular photo frame from one corner and it leans over, but its opposite sides stay parallel. You have made a parallelogram!
points: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal and parallel.
Opposite angles are equal.
Neighbouring (adjacent) angles add up to 180°.
The diagonals bisect each other: they cut each other exactly in half. They are not always equal.
Why? A diagonal splits a parallelogram into two identical (congruent) triangles.
learn.reallife: Folding stools, car jacks and the scissor-lift used to fix street lights all use parallelograms that change shape but keep opposite sides parallel.

items.text: If one angle of a parallelogram is 65°, its neighbouring angle is ___
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are ___

items.q: Diagonal is 14 cm. Length from end to centre?
Neighbouring angles are x and 3x. Find x.

quiz.q: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 65°. What is ∠C?
quiz.explain: ∠A and ∠C are opposite angles, and opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.
steps: ∠A and ∠C are opposite angles of the parallelogram.
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.
quiz.mistake: Thinks opposite angles add to 180° instead of being equal

quiz.q: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 65°. What is ∠B?
quiz.explain: ∠A and ∠B are neighbouring angles, so they add up to 180°. ∠B = 180° − 65° = 115°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all angles of a parallelogram are equal, or subtracts from 90°

quiz.q: The diagonals of parallelogram PQRS meet at O. If PR = 16 cm, how long is PO?
quiz.explain: The diagonals bisect each other, so O is the midpoint of PR. PO = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm.
steps: O is the midpoint of PR
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the diagonals cut each other in half

quiz.q: Two neighbouring angles of a parallelogram are in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the smaller angle?
quiz.explain: Neighbouring angles add to 180°. Split 180° in the ratio 2 : 3: 180 ÷ 5 = 36, so the angles are 72° and 108°.
quiz.mistake: Uses 360° instead of 180° for neighbouring angles (gets 144°)

quiz.q: Joseph's garden gate is a parallelogram with sides 120 cm and 80 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: Opposite sides are equal, so the perimeter is 2 × (120 + 80) = 400 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds only two sides, or multiplies the sides like an area

quiz.q: Which property is NOT always true for a parallelogram?
quiz.explain: In a leaning parallelogram one diagonal is clearly longer than the other. Equal diagonals happen only when it is a rectangle.
steps: Opposite sides equal, opposite angles equal, and diagonals bisecting each other are always true.
Diagonals are equal only when the parallelogram is a rectangle.
So 'The diagonals are equal' is NOT always true.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up 'diagonals bisect each other' with 'diagonals are equal'

quiz.q: One angle of a parallelogram is 90°. What can you say about its other angles?
quiz.explain: The opposite angle is also 90°, and each neighbouring angle is 180° − 90° = 90°. So all four are right angles: it is a rectangle.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that neighbouring angles must add up to 180°

quiz.q: Two neighbouring angles of a parallelogram are (x + 20)° and (2x + 10)°. What is x?
quiz.explain: Neighbouring angles add to 180°: 3x + 30 = 180, so 3x = 150 and x = 50. The angles are 70° and 110°.
quiz.mistake: Sets the two angles equal to each other instead of adding them to 180°

teach.ask: Gappu asks: In a parallelogram, if I know one angle is 70°, how can I find all the other angles?
teach.praise: Opposite angles are equal and neighbouring ones add to 180°, so 70°, 110°, 70°, 110°. Super!
teach.nudge: What do you know about the angle opposite to 70°? And about the angles next to it?

revise.summary: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal and parallel, opposite angles are equal and neighbouring angles add up to 180°. The diagonals bisect each other but are not always equal.
focus: Find all angles of a parallelogram from one angle
Use ratios or expressions for neighbouring angles
Use the fact that diagonals bisect each other
Find the perimeter of a parallelogram
remember: Opposite sides are equal and parallel
Opposite angles are equal
Neighbouring angles add up to 180°
The diagonals bisect each other
traps: Opposite angles are equal; they do not add up to 180°
The diagonals of a parallelogram are not always equal
Neighbouring angles add to 180°, not 360°

learn.hook: Take two identical paper triangles and slide them together. You can make a rectangle, a kite or a parallelogram — depending on how you join them!
points: On a geoboard (pins in a square grid), rubber bands make squares, rectangles, parallelograms, kites and trapeziums. Tilted squares can be made too.
To find the area of a tilted shape on a geoboard, draw a box around it and subtract the corner triangles.
Two congruent right triangles joined along the longest side: turned half-way round, they make a rectangle; as mirror images, they make a kite.
Two congruent triangles joined along any side, one turned half-way round, always make a parallelogram.
Joining the midpoints of the sides of a square gives a smaller, tilted square with exactly half the area.

example.q: A square has side 10 cm. Its side midpoints are joined. What is the area of the new square?
steps: The four corner triangles together make half of it

learn.reallife: Tile and rangoli designs often use squares inside squares made by joining midpoints.

games.title: Join two congruent triangles

Right triangles on the long side, mirror images
Any triangles on a side, one turned round
Midpoints of a square's sides joined

items: You can make a tilted square on a geoboard.
For example, with corners (0,0), (2,1), (1,3), (−1,2).
Joining midpoints of a square's sides gives a rectangle that is not a square.
It gives a square, tilted by 45°.
Two congruent triangles can always be joined to make a parallelogram.
Turn one half-way round and join along a side.
The midpoint square has one quarter of the area of the big square.
It has half the area.

quiz.q: Two congruent right triangles are joined along their longest side, with one turned half-way round. What shape forms?
quiz.explain: The two right angles end up at opposite corners and all four angles become 90°, giving a rectangle.
steps: Turning one triangle puts the two right angles at opposite corners
Each other corner gets the two acute angles, which add to 90°
quiz.mistake: Mixes up turning with flipping (mirror image)

quiz.q: Two congruent right triangles are joined along their longest side as mirror images. What shape forms?
quiz.explain: Mirror images put equal sides next to each other: sides a, a, b, b — that is a kite.
steps: Equal sides meet at the same corner
Two pairs of equal neighbouring sides → kite
quiz.mistake: Assumes every join gives a rectangle

quiz.q: Two congruent triangles are joined along a side, with one turned half-way round. What shape always forms?
quiz.explain: Turning one triangle makes the opposite sides equal, so the shape is a parallelogram.
steps: Turning one triangle half-way round puts each side opposite its equal copy.
So both pairs of opposite sides are equal.
A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides equal is a parallelogram.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the shape must have equal sides all round

quiz.q: A square has side 10 cm. Joining the midpoints of its sides makes a new square. What is its area?
quiz.explain: The four corner triangles fill exactly half of the big square, so the new square is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 cm².
quiz.mistake: Thinks the new square has half the side, so a quarter of the area

quiz.q: Joining the midpoints of a square with side 6 cm makes a new square. What is its area?
quiz.explain: Big square = 36 cm², and the midpoint square has half of it: 18 cm².
quiz.mistake: Takes a quarter of the area

quiz.q: On a geoboard, a rectangle is 3 units long and 2 units wide. What is its area?
quiz.explain: Area = 3 × 2 = 6 square units.
steps: Area of a rectangle = length × width.
quiz.mistake: Adds the sides or finds the perimeter

quiz.q: What shape do you get by joining the midpoints of the sides of a square?
options: A rectangle that is not a square
A kite that is not a rhombus
quiz.explain: All four new sides are equal and all angles are 90°, so it is a square standing on a corner.
steps: Each new side is the long side of a corner triangle
quiz.mistake: Thinks tilting changes the type of shape

quiz.q: On a geoboard, a tilted square has corners at (0,0), (2,1), (1,3) and (−1,2). What is its area?
quiz.explain: A 3 × 3 box around it has area 9. The 4 corner triangles each have area 1. So the square is 9 − 4 = 5.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the whole unit squares inside

teach.ask: Gappu cut two identical triangles from paper. How many different quadrilaterals can he make?
teach.praise: So turning gives a parallelogram (or rectangle), and flipping gives a kite. Paper magic!
teach.nudge: What happens if you turn one triangle round? What if you flip it like a mirror?

revise.summary: Quadrilaterals can be explored on a geoboard and by joining congruent triangles. Two congruent triangles joined with one turned half-way round make a parallelogram, and joining the midpoints of a square gives a tilted square with half the area.
focus: Find areas of tilted shapes on a geoboard by boxing and subtracting
Predict shapes made by joining two congruent triangles
Find the area of the midpoint square
Make squares, rectangles and kites on a geoboard
remember: Two right triangles on their longest side: turned → rectangle; mirrored → kite
Two congruent triangles, one turned half-way round → parallelogram
Midpoint square of a square has half the area
Tilted area = box area − corner triangles
traps: The midpoint square has half the area, not a quarter
Don't expect turning and flipping to give the same shape
Don't count only whole squares inside a tilted shape

learn.hook: The kite you fly at Makar Sankranti and the trapezium-shaped dhol stand both have their own special rules. Let's discover them!
points: A kite ABCD has two pairs of equal neighbouring sides: AB = AD and CB = CD.
In a kite, the diagonal AC (joining the corners where equal sides meet) is the perpendicular bisector of the other diagonal BD. Also ∠B = ∠D.
A trapezium has at least one pair of parallel sides. If AB ∥ DC, the two angles on each slanting side add to 180°: ∠A + ∠D = 180° and ∠B + ∠C = 180°.
An isosceles trapezium has its non-parallel sides equal. Its base angles are equal (∠A = ∠B and ∠C = ∠D), and its diagonals are equal.

example.q: In trapezium ABCD, AB ∥ DC and ∠A = 65°. Find ∠D.
steps: ∠A and ∠D are on the same slanting side
They are co-interior angles, so they add to 180°

learn.reallife: Many bridges and the sides of a handbag are trapeziums; festival kites are, of course, kites!

games.title: Kite or trapezium?
items: Two pairs of equal neighbouring sides
One diagonal is the perpendicular bisector of the other
One pair of opposite angles equal (between unequal sides)
At least one pair of parallel sides
Angles on a slanting side add to 180°
Isosceles type has equal base angles

quiz.q: In trapezium ABCD, AB ∥ DC and ∠A = 65°. What is ∠D?
quiz.explain: ∠A and ∠D are co-interior angles between the parallel sides, so ∠D = 180° − 65° = 115°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the angles on a slanting side are equal

quiz.q: In isosceles trapezium PQRS, PQ ∥ SR and ∠P = 70°. What is ∠R?
quiz.explain: Base angles are equal, so ∠Q = 70°. ∠Q and ∠R are on the same slanting side, so ∠R = 180° − 70° = 110°.
quiz.mistake: Assumes all four angles are equal

quiz.q: In kite ABCD, AB = AD and CB = CD. If ∠B = 100°, what is ∠D?
quiz.explain: In a kite the angles between the unequal sides are equal: ∠B = ∠D = 100°.
steps: In kite ABCD with AB = AD and CB = CD, the angles between the unequal sides are equal.
quiz.mistake: Thinks opposite angles of a kite add to 180°

quiz.q: In kite ABCD (AB = AD, CB = CD), the diagonals meet at O and BD = 12 cm. How long is BO?
quiz.explain: Diagonal AC is the perpendicular bisector of BD, so BO = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.
quiz.mistake: Forgets which diagonal is bisected

quiz.q: In kite ABCD, ∠A = 60° and ∠B = ∠D = 110°. What is ∠C?
quiz.mistake: Thinks ∠A and ∠C must be equal

quiz.q: Which diagonal of kite ABCD (with AB = AD and CB = CD) is cut into two equal halves?
options: AC, the diagonal joining the corners where equal sides meet
BD, the diagonal joining the corners between unequal sides
quiz.explain: AC is the line of symmetry; it cuts BD in half at right angles. AC itself is usually not bisected.
steps: AC is the line of symmetry
Answer: BD, the diagonal joining the corners between unequal sides
quiz.mistake: Thinks a kite's diagonals bisect each other like a parallelogram's

quiz.q: In trapezium ABCD, AB ∥ DC and ∠B is twice ∠C. What is ∠C?
quiz.mistake: Forgets that co-interior angles add to 180°

quiz.q: An isosceles trapezium has parallel sides of 10 cm and 4 cm, and each slanting side is 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: Both slanting sides are 5 cm: 10 + 4 + 5 + 5 = 24 cm.
quiz.mistake: Counts the equal slanting side only once

teach.ask: Gappu is flying a kite with two short sides and two long sides. What special things are true about its diagonals?
teach.praise: So one diagonal is the line of symmetry and cuts the other in half at 90°. My kite flies better already!
teach.nudge: Do the diagonals of a kite meet at a right angle? Which one gets cut in half?

revise.summary: A kite has two pairs of equal neighbouring sides; one diagonal is the perpendicular bisector of the other and the angles between the unequal sides are equal. In a trapezium, the angles on each slanting side add to 180°.
focus: Find angles and lengths in a kite
Know which kite diagonal is bisected
Find angles in trapeziums using co-interior angles
Use the properties of an isosceles trapezium
remember: Kite ABCD (AB = AD, CB = CD): AC is the perpendicular bisector of BD; ∠B = ∠D
Trapezium with AB ∥ DC: ∠A + ∠D = 180° and ∠B + ∠C = 180°
Isosceles trapezium: equal base angles and equal diagonals
traps: A kite's diagonals do not bisect each other
The angles on a slanting side of a trapezium add to 180°; they are not equal
Don't count only one of the equal slanting sides in the perimeter

learn.hook: Is a square a kite? Is a rhombus a parallelogram? Quadrilaterals have a family tree, and some shapes belong to many families at once!
points: Family links: every square is a rectangle and a rhombus; every rectangle and every rhombus is a parallelogram; every rhombus (so every square) is also a kite.
In a Venn diagram, the squares sit where the rectangles and rhombuses overlap, all inside the parallelograms; the rhombuses also sit inside the kites.

Judge by diagonals: bisect each other → parallelogram; equal and bisect each other → rectangle; bisect each other at 90° → rhombus; both → square; one is the perpendicular bisector of the other → kite.
If both pairs of opposite angles are equal, the shape is a parallelogram. Perpendicular diagonals alone do NOT make a rhombus — a kite has them too.

Proof: if AB = CD and BC = DA, draw diagonal AC. Triangles ABC and CDA are congruent (SSS), so ∠BAC = ∠DCA. These are alternate angles, so AB ∥ DC; in the same way AD ∥ BC. So the shape is a parallelogram.

example.q: A rectangle has two neighbouring sides equal. What is it?
steps: A rectangle has 4 right angles and opposite sides equal
Neighbouring sides equal → all four sides equal
4 equal sides and 4 right angles → square

learn.reallife: Sorting shapes into families is like sorting cousins and siblings in a family tree at a wedding!

games.title: Always a parallelogram?
items: Square
Rectangle
Rhombus
Quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides equal
Kite
Trapezium
Quadrilateral with perpendicular diagonals
Quadrilateral with one pair of equal sides

games.title: Family facts
items: Every rhombus is a kite.
Its neighbouring sides are equal in pairs (in fact all four are equal).
Every kite is a rhombus.
A kite can have sides 3, 3, 5, 5.
Equal diagonals that bisect each other always give a rectangle.
That is the rectangle's diagonal property.
Perpendicular diagonals always give a rhombus.
A kite also has perpendicular diagonals.
A square belongs to the rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram and kite families.
It has every one of their properties.

quiz.q: Which family statement is true?
quiz.explain: A rhombus has two pairs of equal neighbouring sides, so it is a kite. The others fail for some shapes.
steps: So AB = AD and CB = CD → kite
Answer: Every rhombus is a kite
quiz.mistake: Reverses a family link

quiz.q: A quadrilateral's diagonals are equal and bisect each other. What must it be?
quiz.explain: Equal diagonals that bisect each other are the mark of a rectangle (a square is a special case).
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the rectangle and rhombus diagonal properties

quiz.q: A quadrilateral's diagonals are perpendicular but do NOT bisect each other. What could it be?
quiz.explain: Rhombuses and squares have diagonals that bisect each other. A kite has perpendicular diagonals where only one is bisected.
quiz.mistake: Thinks perpendicular diagonals must give a rhombus

quiz.q: Both pairs of opposite angles of a quadrilateral are equal. What must it be?
options: A trapezium that is not a parallelogram
quiz.explain: If ∠A = ∠C and ∠B = ∠D, then ∠A + ∠B = 180°, so the opposite sides are parallel — a parallelogram.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the 360° angle sum

quiz.q: To prove that a quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides equal is a parallelogram, which congruence rule is used?
quiz.explain: Diagonal AC gives triangles with AB = CD, BC = DA and AC common — all three sides equal, so SSS.
steps: AB = CD, BC = DA, AC = AC
Answer: SSS, after drawing a diagonal
quiz.mistake: Picks a rule that does not fit the known facts

quiz.q: In the Venn diagram of quadrilaterals, which shapes are in both the rectangle circle and the rhombus circle?
quiz.explain: A shape with 4 right angles and 4 equal sides is a square.
steps: A shape in both circles has 4 right angles (rectangle) and 4 equal sides (rhombus).
4 equal sides and 4 right angles make a square.
So squares are in the overlap.
quiz.mistake: Thinks rectangles and rhombuses never overlap

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT always a parallelogram?
quiz.explain: A kite such as one with sides 3, 3, 5, 5 has no parallel sides. The others always have both pairs of opposite sides parallel.
steps: Rhombuses, rectangles and squares always have both pairs of opposite sides parallel.
A kite with sides 3, 3, 5, 5 has no parallel sides.
So a kite is NOT always a parallelogram.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every symmetric shape is a parallelogram

quiz.q: A rectangle is also a kite. What must it be?
options: A rhombus that is not a square
A rectangle that is not a square
quiz.explain: Being a kite means two neighbouring sides are equal. A rectangle with neighbouring sides equal has all sides equal — a square.
quiz.mistake: Does not combine the two sets of properties

teach.ask: Gappu thinks a square can belong to only one family. How many families does a square really belong to?
teach.praise: A square is a rectangle, a rhombus, a parallelogram AND a kite — it belongs to every family!
teach.nudge: Does a square have all the properties of a rectangle? Of a rhombus?

revise.summary: Quadrilaterals form a family: squares are rectangles and rhombuses, rectangles and rhombuses are parallelograms, and rhombuses are kites. Diagonal and angle properties tell you which family member a shape is.
focus: Decide which family statements are true
Place shapes in a Venn diagram of quadrilaterals
Identify a shape from its diagonal properties
Prove that equal opposite sides make a parallelogram (SSS)
remember: Every square is a rectangle and a rhombus; every rhombus is a kite
Equal diagonals that bisect each other → rectangle
Both pairs of opposite angles equal → parallelogram
Opposite sides equal: diagonal gives congruent triangles (SSS), alternate angles → parallel sides
traps: Perpendicular diagonals alone do not make a rhombus: a kite has them too
A kite is not always a parallelogram
Don't reverse a family link: not every rectangle is a square
